overview: Antigua and Barbuda is a small island country in the eastern Caribbean, made up of two main islands and several smaller ones. Its capital, St. John's, is on Antigua. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1981, and the British monarch is still its head of state. Tourism is by far the biggest part of its economy.

geography.text: Antigua is low and hilly, with a coastline full of bays, beaches and coral reefs; it is often said to have a beach for every day of the year. Barbuda, to the north, is flat and much less populated, and its large lagoon is home to a colony of frigate birds. The islands lie in the path of Atlantic hurricanes.

history.text: Antigua was home to Indigenous Arawak and Kalinago peoples before the English settled it in 1632 and built sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans. Slavery was abolished in 1834. English Harbour became an important base for the British navy. Antigua and Barbuda became independent in 1981.

events.text: English settlers arrive and start sugar plantations.

events.title: Slavery abolished
events.text: Enslaved people are freed across the British Caribbean.

events.title: Hurricane Irma
events.text: The hurricane destroys most buildings on Barbuda.

government.text: Antigua and Barbuda is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor-General, while the Prime Minister leads the government. Parliament has an elected House of Representatives and an appointed Senate. Barbuda has its own council.

economy.text: Tourism is by far the biggest part of the economy, bringing in most of the country's income. Visitors come for the beaches; Antiguans say there is one for every day of the year. Offshore banking and online businesses are also important.

culture.text: Antiguan culture blends African, British and Caribbean traditions. Carnival, held every summer, celebrates the end of slavery with steel bands, calypso and costumed parades. Nelson's Dockyard, a restored Georgian naval base, is a UNESCO site.

items.title: Nelson's Dockyard
items.text: A British naval base from the 1700s, still a working marina.

items.title: 365 beaches
items.text: A popular claim: one beach for every day of the year.

sport.text: Cricket is Antigua's great passion. Viv Richards, one of the greatest batsmen of all time, was born there, and the national stadium is named after him. Sailing Week, held every year since 1968, is one of the Caribbean's top regattas.

items.title: Viv Richards
items.text: West Indies captain and one of cricket's most feared batsmen.

items.title: Antigua Sailing Week
items.text: A regatta held every year since 1968.

didYouKnow: Barbuda's Codrington Lagoon is home to one of the largest frigatebird colonies in the world.
Antigua's English Harbour was once a base for the British admiral Horatio Nelson.
